items.title: Validate envelope structure in decryptBuffer and fail with a clear error on truncated parcels
items.body:
## Problem
`packages/protocol/src/encryption.ts:56-79` (`decryptBuffer`) trusts the envelope header. It reads `keyLength` with `readUInt32BE(0)` and then slices `encryptedKey`, `iv`, `authTag` and `ciphertext` with no length checks. `Buffer.subarray` clamps silently instead of throwing.

- An envelope shorter than 4 bytes throws a bare `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`.
- A truncated or corrupt download (a partial bridge transfer, or a non-encrypted file) gives a short `iv` or `authTag`. The failure then surfaces as an opaque OpenSSL error from `privateDecrypt`, `createDecipheriv` or `setAuthTag`, such as 'Invalid initialization vector' or 'Invalid authentication tag length'.
- A huge `keyLength` swallows the whole buffer, which gives the same confusing downstream error.

Both sync (pull-issue) and reports (Subscription) call this function, so users see these messages when a parcel is damaged or is not an encrypted parcel at all.

## Proposed change
Add a guard at the top of `decryptBuffer`.
- Compute the minimum size: 4 + keyLength + IV_LENGTH + AUTH_TAG_LENGTH.
- If the buffer is shorter than 4 bytes or shorter than that minimum, throw `new Error('Malformed encrypted parcel envelope: ...')`. Say what was expected and what was found.
- Leave the happy path and the envelope format unchanged.
- Add tests to the existing `encryption` test file: an empty buffer, a 3-byte buffer, a truncated real envelope, and a header whose `keyLength` is larger than the buffer. Each must throw the new message. Add a roundtrip assertion to show valid envelopes are unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `decryptBuffer` throws an error containing 'Malformed encrypted parcel envelope' for buffers under 4 bytes.
- [ ] It throws the same error for a truncated envelope and for an oversized `keyLength`.
- [ ] The existing encrypt/decrypt roundtrip tests still pass unchanged.
- [ ] A tampered ciphertext still fails GCM authentication, with the original error type.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass in `packages/protocol`. No file outside `packages/protocol/src` is touched.

items.title: Truncate tool-call arguments in openAiCompatibleRunner's log line so write_file doesn't flood job logs
items.body:
## Problem
`worker/src/modelRunners/openAiCompatibleRunner.ts:174` logs `[tool] ${call.function.name}(${call.function.arguments}) -> ${result.slice(0, 200)}`. Only the result is truncated to 200 characters. The raw `arguments` string is not.

For `write_file` (lines 84-89), `arguments` contains the entire new file content. Every file the model writes is therefore pushed in full through `onOutput`. That reaches `log()` in `worker/src/index.ts:67-70`, where it is batched, POSTed to bridge, and appended with `job.logs += chunk` (see the comment at `index.ts:49-52`). A model rewriting a few large files can add megabytes to a single job's log row. That bloats the DB, makes the Worker page slow, and risks hitting the request body limit on `/logs`, which drops the chunk (`index.ts:61-63` only warns). It also copies task content into logs a second time.

## Proposed change
- Add a small helper in the same file, for example `truncate(text, max = 200)`, that appends `…(+N chars)`.
- Use it on `call.function.arguments` in the log line at line 174 and on `result`, replacing the bare `slice`.
- Do not change what is sent back to the model (line 175) or what `executeTool` receives.
- Add a test with a mocked `fetch` (global stub). The first response requests a `write_file` call with a 50 KB content string. The second response finishes. Assert that the total text passed to `onOutput` is far smaller than 50 KB, and that the file on disk still has the full content.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The `[tool] ...` log line is bounded (arguments at most about 200 chars, result at most about 200 chars) regardless of tool input size.
- [ ] The file written by `write_file` and the `tool` message sent back to the model are unchanged.
- [ ] A new test covers the large `write_file` case.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass in `worker`.

items.title: Fail loudly on malformed or empty OpenAI-compatible responses instead of returning an empty chat reply
items.body:
## Problem
Two response-handling gaps in worker's OpenAI-compatible paths.

1. `worker/src/chatRunners/openAiCompatibleChat.ts:43-47` reads `data.choices[0]?.message.content ?? ''`.
   - If the provider returns an empty or null `content`, for example on a content-filter finish or an unexpected shape, the function returns `''`.
   - `processChatTurn` (`worker/src/index.ts:156`) then calls `client.complete(messageId, '')`. The user sees a blank assistant message, marked as success.
   - If `choices` is missing or `message` is undefined, `data.choices[0]?.message.content` throws a bare `TypeError`. `?.` guards `choices[0]` but not `message`, and nothing guards `choices` itself.
2. `worker/src/modelRunners/openAiCompatibleRunner.ts:144-151` does `data.choices[0]?.message`, so a body without `choices` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')`. That message is reported to bridge as the job's error.

The providers are third-party (gpt, deepseek, qwen) and are routed through a proxy, so non-standard 200 responses are realistic.

## Proposed change
- In the chat path, read `data.choices?.[0]?.message?.content`. If it is empty or whitespace, throw `new Error(`${options.model} returned an empty reply`)`. The existing `catch` in `processChatTurn` will call `client.fail` with that message, so the user sees a real error.
- In the runner, use `data.choices?.[0]?.message`, and keep the existing 'returned no message' error for the missing case.
- Add tests with a stubbed global `fetch`. Cover chat with `{choices: []}`, chat with `content: null`, chat with a normal reply, and the runner with a body of `{}`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `openAiCompatibleChat` rejects with a descriptive error on missing `choices`, missing `message`, and empty or null `content`.
- [ ] A normal reply is returned unchanged.
- [ ] `runOpenAiCompatible` rejects with '... returned no message' when `choices` is absent.
- [ ] New tests cover each case.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass in `worker`.

items.title: Make resolveFileSecrets name the failing key/file and reject empty secret files
items.body:
## Problem
`worker/src/secrets.ts:11-20` (`resolveFileSecrets`) runs once at startup from `main()` (`worker/src/index.ts:171`) and has two weaknesses.

1. `readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8')` at line 18 is unguarded. A wrong Swarm secret path throws a raw `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/run/secrets/...'`. The message does not say which env key (`BRIDGE_API_KEY_FILE`, `OPENAI_API_KEY_FILE`, ...) pointed there. With five secret keys in `SECRET_ENV_KEYS` (lines 22-28), the operator has to guess.
2. An empty or whitespace-only secret file is `trim()`med to `''` and assigned to `env[key]`. Everything downstream tests env values for truthiness (`if (env[key]) continue` here, and the provider config modules). The secret is silently treated as unset, and the failure shows up much later. For example, the worker may start and then fail every request with 401, or report 'API key missing' for a key that is configured but empty.

There is no test file covering this module's failure paths.

## Proposed change
- Wrap the read in try/catch and rethrow `new Error(`Cannot read ${key}_FILE (${filePath}): ${message}`)`.
- If the trimmed content is empty, throw `new Error(`${key}_FILE (${filePath}) is empty`)`.
- Keep the precedence rule: a plain env value still wins and the file is not read.
- Add `secrets.test.ts` (node:test) that uses a temp dir and covers four cases: a file is read and trimmed, plain env wins, a missing file produces an error naming the key and path, and an empty file produces an error naming the key.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A missing secret file error message contains both the env key name and the file path.
- [ ] An empty or whitespace-only secret file throws instead of setting an empty env value.
- [ ] Existing behavior is preserved: plain env wins, an unset `_FILE` is skipped, and file content is trimmed.
- [ ] New tests cover all four cases.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass in `worker`.
